questions.question: You approach a bridge with a "12t" Mass Limit sign. You are driving a truck with a tare weight (empty weight) of 6 tonnes, carrying 5 tonnes of cargo. The truck's registered Gross Vehicle Mass (GVM) on its licence disc is 14 tonnes. Are you allowed to drive across?

options.text: No, because the vehicle's maximum capability (GVM) on paper is 14 tonnes, which exceeds the sign's limit.
Yes, because your actual combined weight right now is 11 tonnes, which is under the 12-tonne limit.
Yes, but only if you drop your speed below 20 km/h before entering the bridge.

questions.question: A light commercial delivery vehicle has a body width of 1.95 metres, but its extended side mirrors add an extra 0.20 metres on each side, bringing the overall total width to 2.35 metres. The route ahead displays a circular sign with a red border containing 2.1m with horizontal arrows pointing inward from the sides. How does this restriction apply legally?

options.text: Proceeding past the sign is strictly prohibited because overall vehicle width includes mirrors and any side projections, which exceeds 2.1 metres.
The vehicle may legally proceed because statutory width limits apply strictly to the fixed wheel track and primary body shell, excluding adjustable wing mirrors.
The vehicle is permitted to enter provided it travels in the centre of the roadway and yields to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A circular regulatory sign features a red border enclosing a white background with two dashes. What is the exact legal application of this prohibition sign?

options.text: No unauthorized motor vehicle may enter or proceed on the roadway beyond the sign, except vehicles explicitly permitted by supplementary plates or authorized personnel.
The roadway is permanently closed to all vehicular traffic without exception, including emergency service vehicles.
Overtaking and passing slow-moving vehicles is prohibited across the two parallel black roadway markings ahead.

questions.question: Approaching an intersection, a driver observes a circular sign with a red border and a diagonal red slash across a black arrow pointing left. Which rule applies at this junction?

options.text: Drivers are legally prohibited from executing a left turn at the immediate intersection ahead, but may proceed straight, turn right, or make a U-turn unless otherwise restricted.
The road ahead curves sharply to the left, requiring drivers to reduce speed to a mandatory minimum limit.
Drivers are legally prohibited from turning left at the intersection, and making a U-turn is automatically authorized as a substitute maneuver.

questions.question: What exact maneuver restriction is enforced at a location where the Right Turn Prohibited sign is displayed?

options.text: It serves as an advance warning that turning right at the next upcoming intersection will be prohibited.
It prohibits making a right turn directly at the point, entrance, or intersection where the sign is posted.
It prohibits making a right turn at the intersection, while simultaneously prohibiting making a U-turn or proceeding straight through.

questions.question: A driver traveling on a two-way single-carriageway road passes a circular prohibition sign featuring two cars side-by-side with a diagonal red bar. A few meters ahead, the driver catches up to a stationary broken-down vehicle blocking the left lane. What is the correct legal application of the sign in this scenario?

options.text: Passing any stationary vehicle or obstruction is completely illegal under this prohibition sign until an "End of Overtaking Restriction" sign appears.
Passing a stationary hazard is legally permitted provided the maneuver can be executed safely, as passing a stationary obstruction does not constitute "overtaking" a moving vehicle.
Overtaking is strictly prohibited for light passenger vehicles, but heavy commercial vehicles may pass provided they flash their hazard lights.

questions.question: You are driving a delivery vehicle with a Gross Vehicle Mass (GVM) of 2,800 kg. You approach a stretch of road displaying the "Overtaking by Goods Vehicles Prohibited" sign and catch up to a slow-moving tractor. Which statement describes your legal obligation?

options.text: You may pass the tractor provided you complete the pass without crossing any solid white line painted on the roadway.
You are strictly prohibited from overtaking any stationary or moving vehicle past this sign until a cancellation sign appears.
You are allowed to overtake because the prohibition sign applies specifically to goods vehicles exceeding 3,500 kg GVM.

questions.question: You are driving down a road and realize you missed your turnoff. Ahead of you is an intersection displaying a "U-Turn Prohibited" sign. However, you see a driveway entrance just before the intersection on your right. Which action is legal under traffic regulations?

options.text: You are strictly forbidden from turning your vehicle around to travel in the opposite direction anywhere on this roadway section or at the intersection.
You may execute a 3-point turn using the driveway entrance, provided you do not proceed into the intersection where the sign is posted.
You may perform a U-turn at the intersection only if a traffic officer explicitly signals you to do so or if traffic lights are out of order.

questions.question: You pass a "Hitch-Hiking Prohibited" sign with a supplementary plate reading "500m". Exactly 200 metres past the sign, you spot your friend waiting safely in a paved lay-by (bus stop area) off the main roadway. What does the law permit you to do?

options.text: You may stop and pick them up, because the restriction only prohibits pedestrians from actively soliciting rides, not drivers from offering them.
You may stop to pick them up only if your vehicle stays fully outside the active driving lane inside a designated lay-by.
You are strictly forbidden from stopping to pick up any passenger on this road section for 500 metres beyond the sign.

questions.question: You pull up next to a curb where a "No Parking" sign is posted. You keep your vehicle's engine running, hazard lights on, and stay sitting in the driver's seat while waiting 3 minutes for a passenger to drop off a parcel. Which statement correctly reflects your legal status?

options.text: You are legally stopped because the engine remains running, you stay in the driver's seat, and the duration is under 5 minutes.
You are violating the law because stopping a vehicle for any period longer than 1 minute constitutes "parking" under road traffic legislation, regardless of whether you remain in the driver's seat.
You are allowed to stop temporarily past this sign, provided you are actively loading or unloading goods or passengers and do not leave the vehicle unattended.
